entries.title: Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky calls it a gift to Putin
entries.snippet: Ukraine's president sharply criticised the move, calling it an "investment in war that must be ended, not prolonged".

entries.title: Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices
entries.snippet: The US president hopes to ease his party's pain before next month's midterm elections, writes the BBC's North America correspondent.

entries.title: US unveils sanctions on ICC in move court condemns as 'assault on rule of law'
entries.snippet: Several member states of the international tribunal, including the UK, say they "strongly disagree" with the sanctions.

entries.title: Thousands of security personnel deployed as Delhi braces for ‘cockroach’ protest
entries.snippet: Several trains to Delhi have been cancelled and dozens of metro stations are shut to stop protesters from gathering.

entries.title: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he will not watch it
entries.snippet: The planned execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

entries.title: Powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake hits Panama, damaging buildings
entries.snippet: Tsunami warnings are issued for neighbouring countries as videos of destruction circulate online.

entries.title: Navi Pillay, former UN human rights chief, wins Nobel Peace Prize
entries.snippet: Pillay is recognised for her "efforts to promote peace and international law", the Norwegian Nobel Committee says.

entries.title: Man named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
entries.snippet: The left-wing candidate won a narrow victory in a remote district in the Peruvian Andes, exit polls show.

entries.title: Three men found guilty of murdering two Australian surfer brothers and US friend
entries.snippet: The bodies of Jake and Callum Robinson and their friend Carter Rhoad were found at the bottom of a well.

entries.title: Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
entries.snippet: Often dubbed "Russia's Google", the tech firm admits customers may experience disruption to digital services due to the attacks.

entries.title: Ethiopia warns Eritrea it will defend itself after troops cross border
entries.snippet: Truckloads of Eritrean soldiers have been seen driving into Ethiopia, which has reportedly responded with drone strikes.

entries.title: Commentator Katie Zacharia picked as new White House press secretary
entries.snippet: The conservative commentator currently works as a communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group.

entries.title: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine worth €5m in Italy, reports say
entries.snippet: The heist at the Florence-based winery is believed to be one of the largest thefts of its kind in Italy.

entries.title: US immigration officials defend ICE agents who shot man in same car as child
entries.snippet: Oscar Belgal, the 28-year-old man, survived the shooting and is now being held at a detention facility outside of New York, officials said.

entries.title: France promises 3,000 extra teachers in first step to calm student protests
entries.snippet: Education minister Edouard Geffray makes the offer after another day of sometimes violent demonstrations by high-school students.

entries.title: Three Saudi nationals killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport
entries.snippet: The missile attacks come amid an escalation in fighting between the Iran-backed group and Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government.

entries.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire speaks to BBC
entries.snippet: Vitalii Zhykovych gives his own account of the attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev.

entries.title: Crazy Rich Asians to return as TV show with original film's stars
entries.snippet: It will pick up after the hit 2018 film, starring Constance Wu, Henry Golding, Michelle Yeoh and Ronny Chieng.

entries.title: Doctor accused of 1994 Rwanda genocide offences to face trial in UK
entries.snippet: Dr Vincent Brown was allegedly a "leader" or "supervisor" of violent acts carried out by others in the early days of the genocide.

entries.title: Two Renoir paintings stolen from French museum are recovered
entries.snippet: The two works were seized last month when thieves cut through a fence and smashed a window at the Renoir Museum on the French Riviera.

entries.title: Kalshi taps former FBI agent to fight against money laundering
entries.snippet: The prediction market company says it wants to prevent its platform from being abused by criminals. The company is facing mounting pressure over market manipulation and insider trading on the site.

entries.title: Fired OpenAI employees question the company's commitment to safety
entries.snippet: The three fired workers say OpenAI punished them for being outspoken about safety. The company disputes the claims and says they were fired over mishandling sensitive information.

entries.title: Trump says U.S. to get diesel from Russia, relaxing pressure on Moscow to ease prices before midterms
entries.snippet: Trump says the U.S. will obtain diesel from Russia, relaxing years of U.S. pressure on Moscow, to combat prices before midterms. He said he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call.

entries.title: The U.S. last held a public execution in the 1930s. The Pentagon wants to change that
entries.snippet: The Pentagon says it will livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan at Fort Hood, the site of his 2009 mass shooting. That would be the first public execution in the U.S. since the 1930s.

entries.title: U.S. working to reverse an Egyptian man's third-country deportation to Africa
entries.snippet: The Trump administration's effort to return Ahmed Soliman to the U.S. come after an Arizona judge said his deportation violated due process.

entries.title: Did Russia play by the rules in reporting lab worker's death?
entries.snippet: A global treaty signed by 197 countries — including Russia — requires reporting any death that could be a sign of an outbreak to come.

entries.title: How the oil industry is preparing for Hurricane Isaias
entries.snippet: Hurricane Isaias is this season's first Atlantic hurricane, and is on a path to hit the northern Gulf Coast. How is the oil industry preparing?

entries.title: Trump says U.S. won't attack Iran before midterms. And, ICE agent shoots man in NYC
entries.snippet: Trump announced that the U.S. will not attack Iran ahead of the midterms. And, a 28-year-old man is receiving treatment at the hospital after an ICE agent shot him in the neck.

entries.title: Why American investors love European defense startups
entries.snippet: As European defense spending takes off, just about half of the funding in Europe's defense tech industry is coming from American investors this year. One reason why: European investment firms have restrictions on how they can invest.

entries.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: A plague research employee in Russia died from ____
entries.snippet: Plus: Nobels! Protests! Ambiguous quotes! A mysterious death in Russia!

entries.title: How local officials are testing voting machines to ensure election integrity

entries.snippet: A Republican donor is accusing U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle of asking for $100,000 in exchange for access to top Trump administration officials. Amna Nawaz speaks with Eric Deters, a former Kentucky congressional candidate, about the requests for payment and the a

entries.title: Brooks and Capehart on the fight for Senate control in battleground states
entries.snippet: Candidates for U.S. Senate in three battleground states faced off in fiery debates Thursday night that frequently veered into personal attacks. David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including the battle for c

entries.snippet: Actor Ke Huy Quan went from arriving in America as a refugee to starring in Indiana Jones and The Goonies. Decades later, he made an Oscar-winning comeback. In the latest episode of our PBS News podcast "Settle In," Amna Nawaz spoke with him about his debut memoir "Never Say Die,

entries.title: Trump strikes deal with Putin for Russian diesel in sharp reversal of U.S. policy ahead of midterms
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump said he has struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.

entries.title: Legal path seems narrow to challenge livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution, experts say
entries.snippet: Broadcasting the event worldwide isn't mentioned in the Army rules governing how rare military executions are carried out. But that doesn't mean there is a viable legal path to oppose it by anyone besides Nidal Malik Hasan.

entries.title: WATCH LIVE: Graham set to debate Senate challengers Andrews, Whitener in South Carolina
entries.snippet: South Carolina Republican Sen. Darline Graham will face off in a debate Sunday against Democratic challenger Dr. Annie Andrews and Libertarian candidate Kasie Whitener.

entries.title: WATCH: Vance says he's 'not going to be watching' livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution
entries.snippet: Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on Friday whether the Pentagon will livestream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan in December but told reporters that if it is livestreamed, "I'm not going to be watching it."

entries.title: Trump establishes committee to investigate Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook in latest effort to fire her
entries.snippet: The inquiry will include a hearing at the White House Nov. 5, President Donald Trump said in a written memo, that Cook "shall" attend to answer questions from the committee.

entries.title: As Blanche hits the campaign trail, new DOJ memo relaxes rules around political conduct for Senate-approved appointees
entries.snippet: The Department of Justice is making it easier for Attorney General Todd Blanche and other Senate-confirmed DOJ appointees to participate in political activities, according to a new internal memo obtained by PBS News.

entries.title: Time for term limits? Dems in majority could have familiar faces in key roles
entries.snippet: Democrats hope to bring a new agenda to the House next year if they take the majority, but they will most likely do so with many of the same faces that have steered their party's legislative work for a decade or more.

entries.title: Trump wants Talarico and Paxton to debate. Talarico couldn't be happier
entries.snippet: When Democratic nominee James Talarico stopped holding campaign events in the Texas Senate race, his Republican opponent Ken Paxton saw an opening to pounce.

entries.title: The midterms stakes are high for these 2028 presidential prospects
entries.snippet: As most of the political world focuses on next month's midterm elections, the shadow primary for the 2028 presidential contest is quietly playing out in public view.

entries.title: WATCH LIVE: Trump rallies with New York's GOP gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman
entries.snippet: At a political moment where Republicans are hoping to capture centrists wary of an ascendent progressive left, Blakeman has instead embraced the president and his aggressive conservative tactics.

entries.title: Trump's memorial arch faces a new lawsuit from Arlington County, Virginia
entries.snippet: The Arlington County Board in Virginia filed a lawsuit Thursday opposing the construction of the Triumphal Arch, becoming the first governmental body to take legal action against President Donald Trump's planned monument.

entries.title: The plague never went away. Cases are reported in parts of Africa and the U.S. nearly every year
entries.snippet: The plague, the rare bacterial infection infamously known for killing tens of millions in 14th-century Europe, never went away. It is now easily treated with antibiotics.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
entries.snippet: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

entries.title: Trump, Putin agree on deal to release Russian diesel to US, world markets
entries.snippet: Russia will supply diesel to global markets in a bid to lower prices, US President Donald Trump has said. The move reverses years of pressure on the Russian economy following the invasion of Ukraine.

entries.title: Strong earthquakes shake Panama, buildings damaged
entries.snippet: Panama's president has declared a "major disaster" after a series of tremors damaged buildings, briefly suspended flights and triggered a tsunami alert in Central and South America.

entries.title: UAE: Omani Flydubai co-pilot planned suicide attack
entries.snippet: A Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight into the terminal at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, according to a UAE official.

entries.title: China, EU reach deal to 'moderate' China's car exports to EU
entries.snippet: An agreement between the EU and China would reduce exports of Chinese electric and plug-in hybrid cars to the 27-member European bloc by up to 50%, according to the EU trade envoy.

entries.title: Brussels: Rioters clash with police at anti-austerity rally
entries.snippet: Violent rioters, many of whom were masked, confronted police at the edge of an anti-austerity march in Brussels. Police responded with water cannons and tear gas.

entries.title: Eritrean troops in Ethiopia raise fears of a regional war
entries.snippet: Ethiopia and Eritrea are trading blame for confrontations in Tigray amid international calls for restraint. Their respective allies have the potential to catapult the conflict into a regional war.

entries.title: Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
entries.snippet: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

entries.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
entries.snippet: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

entries.title: US imposes sanctions aiming to 'dismantle' International Criminal Court
entries.snippet: The US has announced new sanctions on the International Criminal Court. It's the latest in a series of steps by the Donald Trump administration as it seeks to "dismantle" the intergovernmental organization.

entries.title: Saudi coalition vows 'firm' response after airport attack kills 3
entries.snippet: Saudi Arabia and its allied forces in Yemen vowed a "firm response" to Houthi attacks that target civilians. The kingdom's authorities said three Saudi nationals were killed in Thursday's attack on Riyadh airport.

entries.title: Is China seeking to restrict Taiwan's cultural presence?
entries.snippet: From coffee competitions to literature awards, Beijing appears to be working to limit Taiwan's international cultural and political impact.

entries.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
entries.snippet: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.

entries.title: Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
entries.snippet: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

entries.title: India's 'cockroaches' vs Election Commission: What you need to know ahead of CJP's October 10 protests
entries.snippet: The Indian capital New Delhi has been turned into a fortress with train and metro cancelations, barricades and heavy police presence ahead of Saturday's planned protests against the chief of India's electoral body.

entries.title: Hurricane Isaias intensifies en route to US Gulf Coast
entries.snippet: Oil and gas production in the Gulf of Mexico has already been affected by the approaching hurricane, which has strengthened so far to Category 2.

entries.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
entries.snippet: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

entries.title: France: Investigators recover 2 stolen Renoir paintings
entries.snippet: Thieves had initially taken four pieces with a value of over $10 million, but dropped two as they fled. Officials praised everyone that tracked down the paintings, but didn't reveal how they found them.

entries.title: Voting to begin in local elections in the Czech Republic
entries.snippet: The vote is being seen as a test of popularity for Prime Minister Andrej Babis's government.
